If you went back in time, to the 1960s when the space race was in full swing, you would've seen a group of brilliant but sometimes feuding scientists at the forefront of it all. It was called "The Last Card," and it was a perfect example of how a small, seemingly insignificant detail can change everything in a moment. The story went like this:

> 
> It was a cold and wet night in the Russian forest, and Private Jameson was sent to deliver a message to the commanding officer, who was camped deep in the woods. As he trudged through the knee-deep snow, his boots sank in, and his fingers started to freeze. But he pressed on, all the while keeping his eyes fixed on the card he carried, a rare and valuable playing card that his mother had given him before he left for the war.

I think my favorite time at the beach was when my family and I went on a road trip to the Pacific coast, and we decided to take a detour to a little-known spot called Cove Cove. It was a tiny cove, almost hidden from the main highway, but the water there was just magical - crystal clear and filled with all sorts of colorful fish and sea life. We spent the morning swimming and playing in the waves, and then decided to take a walk along the beach to see what else we could find.
